## Structure: tiers, not families
A `tier` is ONE CRATE's wasm32 corpus. It has a full-corpus Worker (every test the crate
registers) and a set of shard Workers that must partition that corpus exactly. The
freshness invariant is stated PER TIER, because the eight crates are eight separate
`cargo build` invocations producing eight separate .wasm files with eight independent
counts.
Stating it per tier rather than over the union is the point, and gets STRONGER with every
tier added, not weaker. If the checker only compared 1719+722+143+111+69+24 against a
single deployed total, a +11 drift in temper-drc-rs cancelling a -11 drift in
temper-geometry would pass -- two stale modules reported green by arithmetic. Per tier,
each crate's deployed count must equal its own built count, so nothing cancels. Note what
the three tiers added on 2026-08-11 do to the union check specifically: 24, 69 and 111 are
each SMALLER than the drift a drc-vs-geometry cancellation can absorb, so under a union
check an entire tier could go missing and the arithmetic would still balance. That case is
pinned in tools/wasm/test_check_deployed_freshness.mjs section C.
## Why the seven single-family crates are their own Workers rather than more tests
## in temper-wasm-tier
1. Each declares exactly one family (`wasm-registry-geometry`, `-thermal`,
`-design-bundle`, `-router-core`, `-constraint-compiler`, `-quality-oracle`,
`-io-types`; see those crates' Cargo.toml): each is a flat set of independent
kernels, parsers or lowering stages with no rule-family taxonomy, so a per-family
split has nothing to split on. temper-quality-oracle's own Cargo.toml comment says
it plainly: "the six-layer quality pipeline is a flat sequence of pure scoring
kernels with no rule-family taxonomy"; temper-io-types's says "what survives
--no-default-features here is a flat set of KiCad/DSN serialisers, parsers and the
placer CONTRACT kernels, with no rule-family taxonomy to shard along".
2. It leaves the existing Workers' bytes, counts, and dependency graphs untouched --
all seven crates are OPTIONAL dependencies of temper-wasm-test-runner precisely so a
drc-only build is unchanged. The drc invariant (temper-wasm-tier == 1719 == the sum of
its 7 shards) therefore keeps its exact prior meaning, and the control that caught the
11-test gap on 2026-08-10 keeps its exact prior bite.
3. One Worker serves both of each crate's roles: it is the tier's full-corpus Worker AND
the single shard sweep_multi_worker.mjs dispatches. So each is +1 Cloudflare script,
not +2.
Note honestly what that costs: each of those tiers' shard set is the singleton {itself},
so its partition check (`shards sum == built`) is the SAME equation as its full-corpus
check and adds nothing. The count check is the whole bite for those tiers, and it is not
degenerate. The partition check regains its independent force the day any of them is
sharded by size.
## Fields
crate              Cargo package whose registry this tier carries. Informational, and
the key callers use to name a tier on the command line.
cargo_features     --features passed to temper-wasm-test-runner to build the full
corpus for this tier. --no-default-features is always also passed.
staged_module      Filename under packages/temper-worker/src/ that
scripts/stage_wasm_families.sh copies the built .wasm to, and that
the Worker entry point imports. Gitignored (.gitignore:141).
full_corpus_worker Cloudflare script name carrying every test in the tier.
wrangler_dir       Directory containing the wrangler.toml for full_corpus_worker.
expected_failures  Manifest of native-vs-wasm32 divergences for this crate. Bundled
into the Worker and passed to run_wasm_tests.mjs / r19_compare.py.
native_test_args   The `cargo test` arguments whose verdicts this tier's wasm32
verdicts are compared against (R19). Debug, not release, for every
tier -- see "Why every native arm is debug" below.
READ, not decoration: .github/workflows/wasm-tier-nightly.yml runs
`cargo test $native_test_args` for every tier in this array. It did
NOT until 2026-08-11 -- the field was documented here while the
workflow spelled out one hand-written step per crate, so editing
this value changed nothing and the two could disagree silently.
That is the same defect this whole file exists to abolish, one
field later, and adding three tiers is what made it worth fixing
rather than tripling.
shards             The per-family Workers. sweep_multi_worker.mjs dispatches THESE;
the full-corpus Worker is not in that fan-out at all, which is why
their counts must sum to the built count independently.
## Why every native arm is debug
temper-geometry FORCED the choice. Measured 2026-08-10 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:
`cargo test --release --no-default-features` fails 1 (778/1) where debug passes 779/0.
The failure is pad_geometry::tests::pow2_is_exact_where_powi_is_not, a staleness guard
asserting that LLVM does NOT fold powi(2, -1024) natively the way it does on wasm32. At
opt-level 3 it does fold, the guard fails on BOTH sides, r19_compare.py scores agree_fail,
and a real divergence stops being reported as one.
temper-thermal PERMITS release and is pinned to debug anyway. Measured 2026-08-10, same
host: `--no-default-features` passes 191/0 in BOTH profiles, and all four of its
b7-pow-divergence-absent guards pass in both. They survive -O3 because
hostmath::pow is a `dlsym`-resolved function pointer -- opaque to LLVM, so there is
nothing to constant-fold, unlike geometry's `powi` intrinsic. That immunity is a property
of hostmath.rs's current implementation, not a guarantee: the day hostmath falls back to
`f64::powf` natively (which is exactly what it already does on wasm32, and the reason
those four tests are in the manifest), release would fold and the guards would fail
natively too -- geometry's failure mode, one crate later. Debug is where the guard has
headroom, it is what the other two tiers already run, and it saves the nightly a second
full x86_64 optimised compile of the dependency graph. There is no offsetting benefit to
release here: no wasm32 verdict depends on the native profile, only the join does.
temper-design-bundle, temper-rust-router-core and temper-constraint-compiler PERMIT
release too, and are pinned to debug for thermal's reasons rather than geometry's. Both
profiles measured 2026-08-11 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, `--no-default-features`, and
both are identical in every respect that could matter -- same pass counts, zero failures,
and (checked, not assumed) IDENTICAL TEST-NAME SETS, so the R19 join is the same join
either way:
temper-design-bundle        debug 26/0   release 26/0   name delta 0
temper-rust-router-core     debug 147/0  release 147/0  name delta 0
temper-constraint-compiler  debug 97/0   release 97/0   name delta 0
So the pin is a deliberate choice among equals, not a forced one, and saying so is the
point: none of these three carries a guard of geometry's kind (an assertion that the
HOST does not do what wasm32 does), which is the only thing that has ever made this
choice load-bearing. What decides it is cost and uniformity -- debug is what the other
three arms run, and release would add a second optimised x86_64 compile of each
dependency graph to every nightly for no verdict that differs. If one of these crates
later grows a float-fold or intrinsic staleness guard, re-measure: `release` acquiring
wasm32's behaviour is exactly how geometry's guard stopped guarding.
## Why every native arm is --no-default-features
For temper-thermal this is load-bearing in a way it is not for the other two: that
crate's DEFAULT feature is `python`, which pulls pyo3 (with `extension-module`) and faer
into a plain `cargo test`. Measured 2026-08-10: the default build passes 198/0 and
`--no-default-features` passes 191/0. The 7-test difference is EXACTLY
`solve::tests::*` (7 tests; the module is `#[cfg(feature = "python")]` at the crate
root, and it is the faer sparse-LU call plus its pyo3 bridge) -- nothing else differs in
either direction. The wasm32 registry cannot contain them, so those 7 are `native_only`
under EITHER invocation and comparing them is not on offer. Paying a pyo3 + faer build
every night to move 7 tests from one native_only bucket to another buys nothing; all 143
wasm32 names are present natively either way (verified: 0 wasm32_only).
The three tiers added 2026-08-11 were measured the same way -- NAME SETS DIFFED, not
counts compared, because a count that matches can still hide a swap, and because
thermal's 7-test gap was only identifiable as `solve::tests::*` by diffing:
temper-design-bundle        default == --no-default-features, exactly. Its `default`
is the EMPTY feature set, so the two invocations are the
same build. 26 names either way, delta 0. The flag is
written out anyway so all six arms read alike and a later
default cannot quietly change what the nightly compares.
temper-rust-router-core     default (`sat`) 164 names, --no-default-features 145.
The 19 lost are EXACTLY `bmc::tests::*` (5),
`equivalence::tests::*` (10) and `solver::tests::*` (4);
nothing is gained in the other direction. Those modules
are `#[cfg(feature = "sat")]` and `sat` pulls
rustsat-cadical, a C++ solver with NO
wasm32-unknown-unknown build -- so the wasm32 registry
cannot contain them under any invocation and all 19 are
`native_only` either way. --no-default-features therefore
costs zero comparison coverage and saves compiling a SAT
solver nightly. All 111 wasm32 names are present natively
(verified: 0 wasm32_only).
temper-constraint-compiler  default (`python` + `sat`) and --no-default-features give
the IDENTICAL 93 names -- delta 0 in both directions. This
is the case where assuming would have been wrong in the
opposite direction from thermal: its default DOES pull
pyo3 and rustsat-cadical, so the expensive build is real,
and it buys not one extra test name. All 69 wasm32 names
are present natively (verified: 0 wasm32_only).
